student_learning_goal: I can analyse data and write a conclusion using mean and mode.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can analyse data and write a conclusion using mean and mode.
header.character_watermark: Detective Dot and Tally with detective hats in the top-right. Small (~1.5in). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Build a frequency table from the survey data.

image_placeholders.description: Survey data + blank frequency table for Grade 3 capstone. Data: 8 student responses to 'favourite recess activity' (e.g., 3 hockey, 2 soccer, 2 tag, 1 hopscotch).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS05_P1_TABLE at Part 1: keywords name the activity.

parts.student_instructions: Build a bar graph (1 unit = 2). Calculate mean and mode of the data.
parts.visual_layout: Blank scaled grid + mean and mode lines.

image_placeholders.description: Blank scaled bar grid + mean/mode lines for Grade 3 capstone. Y-axis 0, 2, 4, 6 (scale 2). Below: 'Mean: ___' and 'Mode: ___' lines.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS05_P2_GRAPH at Part 2: keywords name the activities.

parts.answer_key: Bars at 1.5, 1, 1, 0.5 units (× 2 = 3, 2, 2, 1). Mean: 8÷4 = 2. Mode: hockey OR none.

parts.student_instructions: Write a conclusion using BOTH mean and mode.

image_placeholders.description: A bordered writing box for Grade 3 capstone, ~5in × 1.5in. Above: 'My conclusion (use mean AND mode):'. Below: sentence-frame reminder 'The mode is ___. The mean is ___.'
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS05_P3_CONCLUSION at Part 3: keywords name the activity.

parts.answer_key: Conclusion using both mean and mode. Sample: 'The mode is hockey. The mean is 2 children per category.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write a comparison: 'X is greater than Y by ___.'
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone. Score against rubric. Look for: frequency table (D1.2), scaled graph (D1.3), correct mean and mode (D1.4), conclusion using both (D1.5). Worksheet Parts mirror the 5-station capstone (sort tree, frequency table, bar graph, mean/mode, conclusion). Tune Part 2 data so each bar lands on a whole many-to-one mark (counts 4, 6, 2, 4 with scale 1 unit = 2).
